title: The Crown of Highmoor
premise: Wren Quintana has survived nine years as the crown's food-taster by being forgettable—until a mud-caked child arrives at the palace kitchens speaking Old Highmoor, the language of the realm that was broken and buried beneath the Thornfells. The child is the last heir of Highmoor's hidden court, hunted by those who shattered the ancient covenant between human and fae realms, and Wren's own bloodline as a border-born 'grey child' makes them the only living soul who can carry the reforging oath. As assassins close in and the thirteenth moon wanes, Wren must choose between the crown that owns their life and the belonging they never dared want. In the end, Wren speaks the covenant in two tongues at once, sealing the realms not apart but interwoven—and chooses neither throne nor invisibility, but a new home on the border itself.
about_author: Wren Thornbury grew up in a mining town where three dialects collided in every kitchen, and she credits her ear for untranslatable words to her grandmother's bedtime curses. She writes fantasy about people who belong to borders rather than kingdoms, and this is her second novel.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A routine morning of tasting the king's breakfast establishes Wren's careful invisibility, their immunity built dish by dish, and their secret maps of smuggler roads through the Thornfells. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: Mud on the Kitchen Step
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. During a storm, a feral child appears at the servants' door, speaking a language no one recognizes—except Wren, who half-understands it from lullabies their dead mother sang. Emotional beat: recognition that unsettles everything safe.

chapters.title: Words Older Than Crowns
chapters.summary: Alternating Wren and the child (Iven). Wren hides Iven in the pantry loft and begins piecing together his speech; Iven reveals one word repeatedly: 'covenant.' Emotional beat: tentative trust across a language gap.

chapters.title: The Chancellor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Chancellor Vess's POV. Vess discovers a missing page in the royal archives concerning the Treaty of Ash—a document burned three centuries ago—and suspects someone inside the palace. Emotional beat: cold, methodical menace.

chapters.title: Grey Child
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Iven touches Wren's hand and speaks their mother's name in Old Highmoor, revealing Wren is 'grey-blooded'—born of both realms. Wren denies it, terrified. Emotional beat: identity cracking open.

chapters.title: Thirteen Moons
chapters.summary: Iven's POV. Through fragmented memory-dreams, Iven recalls his flight from the hidden court and the hunters called the Hollow Choir. He explains the deadline: the covenant must be reforged before the thirteenth moon turns. Emotional beat: grief for a slaughtered world.

chapters.title: Poison, Properly Dosed
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A state dinner nearly kills the king; Wren tastes the toxin in time but realizes the poison carries fae signature—someone wants war as pretext to hunt Iven. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Road
chapters.summary: Wren and Iven flee through the Thornfells via Wren's secret paths. Chase sequence with Hollow Choir scouts behind them. Emotional beat: exhilaration of finally using every hidden skill for something that matters.

chapters.title: The Wayhouse at Coldfern
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Sheltering with smuggler allies, Wren learns their mother was a Highmoor envoy who died carrying half of a broken oath-stone. Emotional beat: inherited duty becoming personal inheritance.

chapters.title: Half a Stone
chapters.summary: Iven produces the other oath-half, worn as an amulet. When the halves near each other they sing audibly—but singing attracts the Choir. Emotional beat: hope that is also a beacon.

chapters.title: What the Crown Owes
chapters.summary: Back at court, Chancellor Vess manipulates the grieving king into declaring the fae realm hostile, framing Wren as traitor. Emotional beat: institutional betrayal; the crown Wren served turns its face away.

chapters.title: The Hollow Choir Sings
chapters.summary: Iven's POV. The Choir ambushes the wayhouse; smugglers fall covering their escape. Iven glimpses that the Choir are grey-bloods like Wren who chose servitude to the broken treaty's enforcers. Emotional beat: horror at what Wren could become.

chapters.title: Two Tongues
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wounded and hiding in a cave shrine, Wren finally speaks Old Highmoor aloud—and the mountain answers. Their dual nature stops being a wound and becomes a key. Emotional beat: acceptance of self.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Guided by the stone's song, they find the sunken ruins of Highmoor's court beneath the mountains, alive in pockets of old magic. Emotional beat: awe and sorrow—beauty preserved in exile.

chapters.title: The Last Steward
chapters.summary: An ancient steward tests Wren: the covenant cannot be spoken by a king or a fae lord, only by someone of both blood who chooses it freely. Emotional beat: the weight of being the only door.

chapters.title: Vess at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Vess arrives with soldiers and the captured king's seal, offering Wren pardon in exchange for delivering Iven to be 'contained.' Wren refuses. Emotional beat: love against duty made literal.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Ruins
chapters.summary: A smuggler survivor, coerced by the Choir, reveals their location. Battle in the sunken court; the steward falls buying time. Emotional beat: cost of trust, rage, and sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Moon Rises
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. With the Choir closing in, Wren and Iven reach the covenant altar as the moon crests. Wren must speak the oath knowing it will bind them to the border forever, severing their place at court. Emotional beat: terrified commitment.

chapters.title: Crown of Highmoor
chapters.summary: Climax. Wren speaks the covenant in both tongues; the realms reweave, the Choir unravels into ordinary grieving humans, and Vess's claim dissolves as the old magic acknowledges no crown—only the oath-keeper. Emotional beat: transcendence through choice.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Iven's POV. The hidden court's survivors emerge; Iven, too young to rule alone, asks Wren to stand as steward beside him. The king, humbled, offers Wren honors they decline. Emotional beat: reconciliation without erasure.

chapters.title: A House on the Border
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren builds a small wayhouse where the two realms now meet, feeding travelers from both sides—still a taster, still immune, no longer invisible. Iven visits with stories. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not granted.

chapters.title: The First Guest
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Wren's POV. On the first anniversary, a nervous grey-blooded girl arrives at the wayhouse door speaking a language she was told was shameful. Wren sets a second bowl at the table. Emotional beat: the cycle broken; home as invitation.
